text: Scope SHALL remain SWE.1–SWE.6 and Part 6 clause 5 general topics; no NEW SUP/MAN process workflows, products or assessments.
The product ASIL target SHALL be independently baselined and never inferred or raised from the assurance profile.
Support STANDARD, ENHANCED and HIGH_ASSURANCE project profiles selected by policy, independent of ASIL.
QM work orders SHALL never be described as ASIL compliant; safety-related work orders require approved source allocation and HSI.
ASIL B ++ working index SHALL cover tables 1–15 and distinguish clauses without a methods table.
Normative catalog SHALL keep edition, table, row, A/B/C/D recommendation placeholders, checked status, reviewer, source provenance and footnote/application notes.
An unverified normative catalog SHALL NOT justify an ISO 26262 compliance declaration or safety release, and normative-required evidence unresolved SHALL block an assurance READY claim.
An applicability decision SHALL classify every selected method as APPLICABLE, NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_RATIONALE, ALTERNATIVE_SELECTED, NOT_SUPPORTED or UNKNOWN and retain approver/provenance.
ASIL B ++ SHALL be interpreted according to table alternatives and applicable section requirements; no blind all-methods-mandatory rule.
Existing Automotive SPICE 4.0 SWE baseline SHALL be preserved unless separately approved; no fake CL3/CL4 achievement.
An assurance method catalog change SHALL be baselined, reviewed and reflected in affected claims, without modifying old sealed archives.
STANDARD SHALL preserve existing gates; ENHANCED adds independent assurance checks; HIGH_ASSURANCE adds scoped formal/deeper verification after feasibility checks.
Separate product author, inspection agent, oracle creator, deterministic verifier, gate authority and external reviewer identities or trust domains.
An AI-generated PASS, test name, file presence or artifact count SHALL NEVER suffice for assurance gate PASS.
Oracle sources SHALL be immutable approved requirements/HSI/hardware semantics and SHALL NOT be derived solely from implementation under test.
Hidden holdout fixtures, requirements and expected outcomes SHALL remain inaccessible to candidate and code author roles.
Each verification claim SHALL link an actual executed tool result (name/version/argv or adapter id/exit/digest/time/environment) or a controlled documented review.
Unobserved results SHALL be UNKNOWN/NOT_RUN/NOT_APPLICABLE with rationale, never turned into zero or PASS.
The assurance evaluator SHALL verify provenance, evidence digest, frozen revision, method applicability and independence before accepting a claim.
Failed or incomplete checks SHALL create precise issue codes and provenance; no safety-gate bypass through time/token retry exhaustion.
Evidence and decisions SHALL be append-only with allowed supersession; reinspection SHALL never overwrite first-pass outcomes.
Tool confidence claims SHALL distinguish partial MISRA checks, actual tools, covered rules, exceptions, and qualified-tool evidence when applicable.
Claims SHALL record direct counterevidence and defeaters; unsupported/contradictory claims shall not be silently closed.
Every build and gate SHALL bind a factory revision, profile hash, method catalog hash, requirement baseline hash and target/toolchain identity.
SWE.1 SHALL check unambiguous testability, completeness, internal consistency, time bounds, safe-state behavior and source-provenance for each allocated requirement.
SWE.1 SHALL generate a machine-checkable two-way mapping between requirements, derived tests and source references.
SWE.1 semantic AI review SHALL cite approved source excerpts; contradictory interpretations SHALL open findings rather than invent requirements.
SWE.1 safety requirement gaps SHALL BLOCK safety-scoped packages; QM inapplicability requires scoped rationale.
SWE.2 SHALL check architectural unit allocation, typed interfaces, cohesion/coupling, resource/IRQ ownership, scheduling and shared-resource guards.
SWE.2 SHALL reconcile static/dynamic PlantUML views with component IDs and requirements without treating rendering success as semantic proof.
SWE.2 SHALL include appropriate control-flow, data-flow and scheduling analyses where supported, marking estimates or unsupported tools explicitly.
SWE.2 SHALL provide reasoned interface/architecture inspection independent from architecture author, plus deterministic structural checks.
SWE.3 SHALL enforce low complexity, constrained C constructs, initialization, naming, pointer rules and explicit type conversion via versioned policy and measured analyzers.
SWE.3 SHALL map generated MCU accesses to baselined reference manual/errata including register access semantics, bit fields, reset and side effects.
SWE.3 SHALL detect writes to read-only registers, undefined bits, unsupported register addresses and contradicted simulated peripheral semantics.
SWE.3 SHALL verify reentrancy, concurrency, interrupt execution constraints, timing/timeout and state-transition behavior where applicable.
SWE.3 SHALL output actual static-analysis, MISRA scope/rule coverage, deviation justifications and tool assurance gaps, never infer full MISRA compliance from a partial Cppcheck subset.
SWE.3 SHALL track Flash/RAM/stack/timing budgets by host/simulator/target and by MEASURED/ESTIMATED/UNKNOWN evidence provenance.
SWE.3 SHALL support optionally feasible formal/semiformal proof obligations (e.g., CBMC) on critical low-level operations and report bounded assumptions.
SWE.3 SHALL reject fabricated APIs, missing interface implementations, code not corresponding to detailed design, and changes to frozen tests.
SWE.4 unit tests SHALL derive independent executable expected behavior for positive, negative, boundary and interface conditions from approved requirements.
SWE.4 SHALL prove test cases exercise the allocated API and not only harness/stub code; ambiguous trace-to-call mappings SHALL fail.
SWE.4 SHALL compute statement and branch coverage with justified gaps; never fabricate 100% thresholds attributed to ISO.
SWE.4 enhanced profile SHALL execute a controlled mutation campaign and report eligible/killed/surviving/invalid/equivalent mutants and evidence; thresholds are project policy.
SWE.4 MAY apply selected MC/DC when technically feasible/risk-justified; report that MC/DC is not ++ for ASIL B.
SWE.4 SHALL prevent agents from altering reference-oracle expected results or holdout fixtures to turn failures into passes.
SWE.5 SHALL verify interface integration with requirements-derived, equivalence, boundary, negative, timing and resource-use cases.
SWE.5 enhanced profile SHALL exercise and independently verify relevant fault injection and concurrency/interrupt recovery cases.
SWE.5 SHALL distinguish host, emulator/functional simulation, Renode peripheral model, HIL and actual MCU, including fidelity limitations and expected outcomes.
SWE.5 SHALL support back-to-back model/code comparisons when applicable and justify exclusions.
SWE.5 SHALL verify raw tool outcomes (including Renode), ensure no test-output-only passing without intended target behavior, and open findings for incomplete fidelity.
SWE.5 SHALL ensure integration coverage and requirement trace reports cite immutable executed artifact IDs rather than agent narratives.
SWE.6 SHALL verify real requirement-observing tests against approved requirements and operational use cases, with negative/degraded/transition scenarios.
SWE.6 SHALL distinguish genuine physical HIL/ECU network evidence from simulator results; missing required target evidence produces an honest blocker.
SWE.6 SHALL capture test environment and observability limitations per requirement, including what behavior cannot yet be demonstrated.
SWE.6 SHALL compute requirement coverage from real executed assertions/measurements and expose uncovered or weakly observed items.
Every project SHALL have a structured Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE) graph linking requirements, methods, verification, limitations and counterevidence.
Assurance cases SHALL maintain supported/unsupported/contested state; no AI self-signed safety claim or fabricated ISO 15026-2 certification.
Assurance Gate SHALL aggregate per-phase claims without trading coverage/quality/safety against throughput, token cost or other KPIs.
The Release Manager SHALL include versioned method selection, applicability, oracle evidence, test/coverage/mutation results, assurance case, deficits and hashes in offline review packages.
The factory SHALL output READY_FOR_OFFLINE_REVIEW or BLOCKED only under existing independent policy, and never label automatically ASIL_B_APPROVED.
Safety-specific mandatory supporting documentation missing (e.g., software safety analysis or tool assurance evaluation) SHALL block safety-scoped READY; QM inapplicability may be documented.
Changes to requirements, implementation, tools, prompts or test oracles SHALL trigger explicit impact revalidation of dependent verification and CAE nodes.
SWE.1–SWE.6 gates SHALL retain first-pass/rework states, independent inspector identity and phase revision binding.
Feature 006 SHALL audit archived LL r101 and HAL r102 without mutating their workspaces/archives and report claims that cannot be substantiated from available bytes.
Feature 006 SHALL preserve current 001–005 behavior in OBSERVE_ONLY mode and shall not silently promote CRE/AFO authorization.
Deployment SHALL progress OBSERVE_ONLY -> PILOT -> ENFORCING based on evidence, explicit authorization and independently verified non-regression.
A non-computable metric or absent hardware/tool dependency SHALL show a blocked or inapplicable reason rather than synthetic passing evidence.
Negative tests SHALL prove that forged PASS, stale hashes, poisoned lessons and correlated oracle contamination are rejected.
All 47 ASIL B ++ working-index entries SHALL have mapping to methods/evidence applicability and a baseline verification process.
Project compliance SHALL not be claimed from an internal checklist or ASPICE gate PASS; published result is bounded assurance evidence.
Existing repo safety constitution, credentials, historical baselines and release policies SHALL remain protected from autonomous edits.
